input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: § 11.3 is the only right in the Agreement to examine Customer's use of the Services and Content (compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy under § 11.2(b)); there is no other audit, inspection or verification clause (no hits for audit/inspect/verify/records). As drafted the investigation right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice to Customer (the notice in p0137 is only a best-efforts attempt and applies solely before IBM restricts access or removes Content, not before investigating), allocates no cost, imposes no confidentiality on investigators and does not exclude access to Customer systems. That is unlimited and unannounced examination, i.e. walk-away territory, so it fails the fallback on frequency, notice and cost. Redline adopts the fallback (once per twelve months, 15 days' notice, IBM's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%, no system access) rather than the preferred 30-day/5% formulation, because a 30-day wait would be disproportionate in the context of suspected unlawful Content on IBM-hosted infrastructure.

ops.oldText: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
ops.newText: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b), provided that any such investigation will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon at least fifteen (15) days' prior written notice to Customer, during normal business hours, by an independent investigator bound by written obligations of confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%) of amounts due, and without direct or remote access to Customer's systems or Customer Components.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added the standard guardrails on investigations of our use: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on fifteen (15) days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent investigator under confidentiality, at IBM's cost unless an underpayment above 10% is found, and with no access to our systems. Our playbook does not permit unlimited or unannounced audits or vendor access to Customer systems; we are happy to discuss a shorter notice period where IBM has a good-faith, documented suspicion of unlawful Content.
proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice, cost and no-system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3
